newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil business outlook bullish - Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Brazil business outlook bullish - Reuter poll.

text.p: Brazilian businesses are bullish about the country's economy and most expect sales to grow over the next two years, according to a Reuters poll released on Tuesday.

The survey of 348 businesses, conducted for Reuters by Zogby International from June 23 to July 11, said nearly 70 percent of respondents believe sales would grow in 1997, compared to just 3.7 percent who said sales would decline.
The Reuters-Zogby Brazil Business Confidence Index Survey will be released every six months and is intended to serve as a benchmark for Brazilian business performance.
The poll, which has a margin of error of plus or minus 5.7 percent, found Brazil's business outlook for 1998 even more promising.
Nearly 80 percent of businesses surveyed said sales would rise in 1998, compared to about 3.0 percent that said sales would decline.

Positive sales expectations were based on a widely held view that the economy would expand, the poll said. It said almost 84 percent of respondents saw the economy growing over the next two years compared with just 2.0 percent that saw contraction.
But the level of optimism did not extend to jobs growth. Just 44 percent said they would add jobs in 1997 compared to about 41 percent that said they would keep the same number of employees.

Jobs growth would be less impressive in 1998, according to the poll. About 35 percent of respondents said they would add jobs that year compared with 47 percent who said staff levels would stay the same and 16 percent who said they would cut jobs.
"Employment will not track rising sales due to excess capacity previously (unused) and increased productivity as technological advances are introduced to the workplace," Zogby concluded.
The Brazilian government also drew high marks, with 56.6 percent saying government policy toward business improved over the past five years and 80 percent expecting it to improve in the future.
Businesses were also confident Brazil's stock market would continue to rally in 1998, with 45 percent expecting share prices to rise and just 4.3 percent expecting them to decline.
The poll also surveyed businesses on a number of economic indicators and found that most believe Brazil is heading in the right direction.
It said businesses were optimistic about credit rates, with 52 percent believing long-term interest rates would fall in 1998.

Inflation, which had haunted Brazil for years, has fallen to single digits this year. Thirty-seven percent think inflation will fall further and 48 percent thought inflation would remain steady through the remainder of the year.
Inflation prospects improve next year, with 40 percent of businesses expecting a decline and 38 percent anticipating the same rate of inflation at about 7 percent a year.
